scope.description: Architecture selection for a security threat model of the eShop reference application (AdventureWorks), .NET Aspire services-based e-commerce system.
in_scope: Identity.API, Catalog.API, Basket.API, Ordering.API, OrderProcessor, PaymentProcessor, Webhooks.API, WebhookClient, WebApp, mobile-bff
RabbitMQ event bus and shared Postgres/Redis
objectives: Choose one primary architecture and bounded secondaries for a design-level security review
assumptions: Evidence is source at revision 913acea as reported by the session context
REVIEW_SCOPE is security; no methods or privacy profiles
limitations: Selection only: no threats, controls, treatments or verification were created.
Git was not used; working-tree state not checked.
Complete bodies of selected prompts were not read at selection time (gap G-sel-availability).
Secondary identity-federation and agentic-ai chains are recommended, not scheduled in this run.

evidence.statement: AppHost wires identity, basket, catalog, ordering, order-processor, payment-processor, webhooks, webhooksclient and webapp projects to one Postgres server (four databases), Redis and one RabbitMQ eventbus; mobile-bff is a YARP proxy.
evidence.limitations: Configuration observation only; deployed topology not observed.

evidence.statement: Only identity-api, mobile-bff and webapp use WithExternalHttpEndpoints; other services have none in the AppHost.
evidence.limitations: ACA ingress behavior after deployment not observed.

evidence.statement: mobile-bff routes /api/catalog/{*any}, /api/orders/{*any} and /identity/{*any} to internal services with no HTTP method match in the configuration read.
evidence.limitations: Effective generated YARP config not observed.

evidence.statement: Catalog PUT/POST/DELETE item routes have no authorization and Catalog.API registers no authentication.
evidence.limitations: Absence established by text search of Program/Extensions/Apis only.

evidence.statement: Shared JWT bearer setup disables audience validation and HTTPS metadata requirement; omits authentication entirely when the Identity section is absent.
Ordering routes require an authenticated caller but get, cancel and ship operate on client-supplied order numbers without owner or role checks; create takes UserId from the body.
Basket gRPC derives the basket key from the token subject only; GetBasket is AllowAnonymous.
Webhooks.API issues an OPTIONS request to a caller-chosen URL and later POSTs to caller-chosen destination URLs.
In-memory IdentityServer clients with sample secrets, one client without PKCE, implicit-flow Swagger clients, and scopes not defined as ApiScopes.
evidence.limitations: Secret values redacted from the bundle.

evidence.statement: IdentityServer runs with developer signing credential and key management disabled; seed and migrations run at startup.
WebApp registers model-invocable tools that return user claims, search the catalog and modify the user's basket.
evidence.limitations: Active only when a chat model connection is configured (Foundry opt-in).

evidence.statement: One shared RabbitMQ exchange; events are JSON without sender identity or signature and are dispatched to handlers by event type name.
evidence.limitations: Partial file read; broker ACLs not observed.

evidence.statement: Payment outcome is produced from a configuration flag without a payment gateway call.

Server-side outbound request boundary; egress policy unmapped.

coverage.reason: Run configuration only, not analysis: REVIEW_SCOPE security; METHODS []; PRIVACY_PROFILES []; deep stages 00-05 on deep/microservices; no methods scheduled; secondary architectures are recommendations only.
Selection-only scope: chooses primary and secondary architectures; no threats, treatments or verification created; no prior analysis carried.

Primary architecture is exact ID microservices. Objective: decide security posture of a service-oriented e-commerce reference system whose dominant risks are inter-service authority, edge exposure and shared event/state. Evidence E1, E2, E3, E4, E7, E19, E20. Limits: deployed topology unobserved.

Bounded subsystem: Identity.API client registry, token validation defaults and WebApp/MAUI/WebhookClient OIDC settings; boundary B-token-trust. Added value: token audience/scope/PKCE and client-credential handling not covered by microservices stages. Exclusions: account linking, external IdP flows, Razor views. Evidence E6, E14, E15. Relative effort: one pass per client registration and per resource service. Availability: frontmatter and README read; body unread.

Bounded subsystem: WebApp chatbot tools and model provider; boundary B-model-tools. Added value: model-driven tool authority and claim disclosure. Exclusions: model provider internals, catalog embedding generation. Evidence E18. Relative effort: one pass per tool. Active only when Foundry/Ollama configured. Availability: README read; body unread.
Observed runnable content: deep/microservices stages 00-05 and quick/microservices.md exist in the library checkout; README and frontmatter read. Full bodies read at execution.
Library directory and README observed; complete stage bodies unverified.
Library directory and README observed; complete stage bodies unverified.

Quick baseline: one quick/microservices pass over the bundle. Deeper follow-up: six deep stages on the primary (this run), then optional per-crossing passes for identity-federation and agentic-ai secondaries. Prerequisites: SYSTEM_UNDER_REVIEW plus deployment manifests (G-ub1..G-ub4). Decision value: separates unauthenticated and mis-scoped service authority from infrastructure hardening. Omitted: no duration guarantee, no excluded-family analysis.

Excluded as primary: web (browser/session issues are real but secondary to inter-service authority; WebApp covered through boundaries), event-driven (events are an element of microservices here), payments-transactions (payment is simulated, E20), multi-tenant-saas (no tenant model observed), cicd-supply-chain (workflows are minimal, E25 in bundle), mobile (client code only partially read).

Evidence collected freshly this run at revision 913acea (from session context): listed files read in full or partially; unread service areas, dependency manifests and Git state are recorded in unprocessed_inputs and gaps G-sel-git; coverage is bounded, not exhaustive.
